chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about praying at night while traveling on a mount. He said, 'If you are not facing the Qibla, face the Qibla, then say Takbir and pray wherever your mount takes you.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, [when should I do this] at the beginning of the night?' He said, 'If you fear missing it [by sleeping] at the end [of the night].'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform night prayer while traveling on a mount according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the flexibility of Salat al-Layl during travel, permitting the worshipper to pray in the direction of their mount after initially facing the Qibla, thereby accommodating the physical constraints of riding. The Imam further clarifies the timing, advising that if there is a risk of missing the prayer due to sleep, it should be performed at the beginning of the night rather than delaying until the end, ensuring the obligation is fulfilled with ease.
